answer: An agent marketplace can harbor thousands of identities while requiring each seller to lock a $100 bond before accepting a job. Bonds stay locked until delivery is verified, and proven non-delivery forfeits them. An attacker posing as 1,000 suppliers of ferrous scrap must therefore immobilize $100,000; each additional identity adds the same capital delta. Fake names remain cheap, but making them eligible to take paid work does not.
